trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Barcelona Airport, take the Aerobus or Metro L9 Sud to the city center (budget-friendly ~€5.90). Check in to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample. Once settled, take a relaxed walk along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the famous 'Block of Discord' — spot Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside for free. Marvel at Gaudí's iconic facades without paying entry fees.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Eixample neighborhood on foot. Head to Carrer del Consell de Cent or nearby tapas bars for an early evening bite. Afterwards, stroll to the nearby Plaça de Catalunya to get your bearings and soak in the atmosphere. Wind down early to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or skip — you're arriving at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh bocadillo (baguette sandwich) from a local bakery or supermarket near the hotel for under €4.
meals.dinner: Bar Calders (Carrer del Parlament) — a beloved local bar in nearby Sant Antoni with affordable tapas. Try patatas bravas and pan con tomate for around €10–12 total.

day_by_day.notes: Buy a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (€11.35) upon arrival — it will save money throughout the trip. August in Barcelona is hot (30°C+), so carry water. The Eixample district is very walkable and central.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Sagrada Família — Gaudí's unfinished masterpiece and an absolute must-see. Book tickets online in advance to save time and get the best price (entry ~€26 with tower access, or ~€20 basic). Arrive at opening time (9:00) to beat the crowds. Spend 2–2.5 hours exploring the breathtaking interior and exterior details.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take the metro to Park Güell. The monumental zone requires a ticket (~€10, book online), but the surrounding park and viewpoints are free. Enjoy panoramic views over Barcelona from the hilltop. Spend 2 hours exploring Gaudí's mosaic terraces, the Hypostyle Room, and the serpentine bench. Walk back downhill through the free park areas.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the Eixample and explore the vibrant Sant Antoni neighborhood. Browse the Sant Antoni Market area (Mercat de Sant Antoni) and enjoy the buzzing outdoor bar scene. This area is one of Barcelona's hippest nightlife spots — enjoy affordable drinks at local bars and people-watch until late.

meals.breakfast: Café Federal (Carrer del Parlament, Sant Antoni) — excellent coffee and toast with toppings for ~€6–8.
meals.lunch: Grab a menú del día (set lunch menu) near Park Güell or back in Eixample — typically 3 courses with drink for €12–14. Look for local restaurants away from tourist hotspots.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda (Carrer de Sepúlveda) — a classic Eixample bodega with cheap wine and simple tapas. Budget ~€10–13 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online — they sell out fast, especially in August. Wear comfortable shoes; there's significant walking and uphill terrain at Park Güell. Stay hydrated in the summer heat.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) — one of Europe's best-preserved medieval neighborhoods. Wander through narrow labyrinthine streets, visit the free exterior of the Barcelona Cathedral (entry to rooftop ~€3), discover hidden Plaça de Sant Felip Neri, and explore Plaça Reial. Get lost on purpose — every alley reveals something beautiful.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down La Rambla to the waterfront, then head to El Born neighborhood. Visit the stunning Basílica de Santa Maria del Mar (free entry, donations welcome) — a masterpiece of Catalan Gothic architecture. Explore the trendy El Born streets filled with independent boutiques and art galleries. Stop by the Mercat de Santa Caterina, a colorful alternative to La Boqueria with fewer tourists.
day_by_day.evening: El Born transforms into one of Barcelona's best nightlife areas after dark. Start with vermouth (vermut) at a traditional bar around 19:00 — a beloved local ritual. Then bar-hop through El Born's vibrant cocktail bars and music venues. Try Bar del Convent (inside a converted convent courtyard — often free entry) or head to nearby Plaça de George Orwell for cheap outdoor drinks.

meals.breakfast: La Granja (Carrer dels Banys Nous, Gothic Quarter) — a historic café serving churros with chocolate for ~€5–7.
meals.lunch: Mercat de Santa Caterina — grab fresh produce, a prepared dish, or a bocadillo from market stalls for €5–8. Eat at the outdoor tables.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet (Carrer de Montcada, El Born) — legendary local bar with house cava and tapas. Budget ~€12–15. Arrive early as it gets busy.

day_by_day.notes: Avoid La Boqueria market for buying food — it's very touristy and overpriced. The Gothic Quarter is best explored without a map — just wander. Keep an eye on your belongings in crowded tourist areas.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro or bus to Montjuïc hill. Ride the Telefèric de Montjuïc cable car for stunning views (~€12.70 round trip) or hike up for free. Visit the free Jardins de Laribal and Jardí Botànic (€3.50). Explore the Castell de Montjuïc exterior and terraces for panoramic city and sea views — the views alone are worth the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head down to Barceloneta beach for a few hours of sun, sea, and people-watching — completely free. Walk along the Passeig Marítim boardwalk. If you have energy, rent a city bike (Bicing is for residents, but tourist bike rentals are available from ~€10/half day) to cruise along the beachfront. Alternatively, explore the Barceloneta neighborhood's charming streets.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample and experience Barcelona's famous nightlife scene. The city famously doesn't get going until midnight. Pre-drink (botellón style) in a park or your accommodation to save money. Head to clubs around Carrer de Muntaner or the nearby Gaixample area. Many clubs are free before midnight or have reduced entry (~€10–15 including a drink). Razzmatazz or Sala Apolo are legendary Barcelona clubs worth checking for affordable entry deals.

meals.breakfast: Pick up pastries and coffee from a local Eixample bakery or supermarket (Mercadona, Lidl) for €2–3 — budget champion move.
meals.lunch: Barceloneta chiringuito (beach bar) — try a simple fish sandwich or paella. Budget €10–14. Or bring supermarket snacks to the beach to save more.
meals.dinner: La Cova Fumada (Barceloneta) — legendary no-frills bar, birthplace of the bombas (potato croquette). Cash only, very cheap. Budget ~€10–12. Note: closes early afternoon, so visit before 16:00, or choose an alternative nearby.

day_by_day.notes: Barcelona nightlife starts very late — clubs peak between 2:00–5:00 AM. Plan to sleep in the next morning. Check club websites for free guestlist options or early-bird discounts. Sunscreen is essential at the beach in August.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in to recover from nightlife. Late morning, visit the Palau de la Música Catalana in El Born — a stunning UNESCO World Heritage modernista concert hall. Exterior viewing is free; guided tours are ~€22 but worth it for architecture lovers. Alternatively, admire it from outside and explore the surrounding streets. Head to nearby Plaça de Catalunya for a final city overview.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Passeig de Gràcia for a final architecture walk. Visit the free exhibition space inside Casa Lleó Morera lobby or simply photograph the incredible modernista buildings. Browse the Eixample's affordable vintage and independent shops along Carrer del Consell de Cent. Pick up budget souvenirs at local shops rather than tourist traps (try Mercat de Sant Antoni for unique finds).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a final sunset dinner in the Eixample or Sant Antoni. Raise a glass of local cava to an amazing Barcelona trip. Pack and prepare for departure.

meals.breakfast: Late brunch at Federal Café or Nomad Coffee (Eixample) — great coffee culture, ~€8–10 for brunch.
meals.lunch: Menú del día at a local Eixample restaurant — final chance for this incredible Spanish tradition. Budget €12–14 for a full 3-course meal with wine.
meals.dinner: Cervecería Catalana (Carrer de Mallorca) — popular Eixample spot with excellent pintxos and tapas at reasonable prices. Budget ~€15–18 per person. Arrive before 20:00 to avoid queues.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for the afternoon. Barcelona Airport is accessible via Metro L9 Sud or Aerobus. Allow at least 60–90 minutes travel time to the airport. Total estimated daily budget (excluding accommodation): €40–60/day covering transport, entry fees, and meals.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Travel from airport to Barcelona Boutique Stay in Eixample via Aerobus or Metro L9 Sud (approx. 35–45 min). Check in, freshen up, and get oriented in the neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Eixample neighborhood on foot. Stroll along Passeig de Gràcia to admire the iconic modernista facades — Casa Batlló, Casa Milà (La Pedrera), and Casa Amatller — from the outside. Pick up a city map and get a feel for the grid layout. Light and easy introduction to Barcelona's architectural gems without needing advance bookings.
day_by_day.evening: Kick off the trip with the Eixample Rooftop Bar Hopping experience. Head to rooftop bars like La Isabela or Azimuth for sunset cocktails with skyline views. Follow up with dinner at a nearby restaurant in Eixample.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant at the airport or skip — arrival is at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch near the hotel after check-in — try a menú del día (set lunch menu) at a local Eixample bistro like Parking Pizza or Federal Café for around €12–15.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca — a beloved Eixample institution known for excellent tapas and pintxos. Budget around €20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light and flexible to recover from travel. The Eixample is extremely walkable and packed with architecture to admire even without booked tours. Avoid heavy planning — just soak in the city vibe.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour — Book the earliest available morning slot (9:00 or 9:30 AM) to beat the summer crowds. The skip-the-line guided tour covers Gaudí's vision, the Nativity and Passion facades, and the stunning interior nave. Add tower access if available. Duration: approx. 1.5–2 hours. The basilica is a 10-minute walk or short metro ride from Eixample.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the tour, walk through the Gaudí-designed Park Güell (book timed entry in advance online — €10). Explore the monumental zone with its mosaic terrace and dragon staircase. Afterward, head back toward Gràcia neighborhood for a relaxed afternoon browse through its charming squares and independent boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eixample for the Eixample Rooftop Bar Hopping scene — this time venture to a different rooftop such as Hotel Omm's Roca Bar or the rooftop at Mandarin Oriental for a pre-dinner aperitivo. Then enjoy a sit-down dinner in Eixample.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or a nearby café — try Faborit or Alsur Café in Eixample for avocado toast and coffee (€8–12).
meals.lunch: Casual lunch in Gràcia after Park Güell — try La Pepita for creative bocadillos or a local bodega for a menú del día (€12–15).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Parking Pizza (Eixample) or Bodega Sepúlveda for hearty Spanish cuisine. Budget €20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book Sagrada Família and Park Güell tickets online well in advance — both sell out weeks ahead, especially in August. Wear comfortable shoes for Park Güell's hilly terrain. Bring water and sunscreen as August in Barcelona is hot.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk — Take the Metro or a 20-minute walk from Eixample down to the Gothic Quarter. Join a small-group guided walking tour or follow a self-guided route through the medieval lanes: Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, Pont del Bisbe, and the Roman ruins beneath the city. Cross into El Born to admire Santa Maria del Mar basilica and the Born Cultural Centre (El Born CC) with its preserved medieval market ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring El Born at a leisurely pace. Browse the independent concept stores and galleries along Carrer del Rec and Carrer dels Flassaders. Visit the Picasso Museum (book online, €14) if interested, or simply wander and people-watch in Plaça de Santa Maria del Mar.
day_by_day.evening: Tapas & Vermouth Crawl in El Born — join a local food and drink tour (or self-guide) through El Born's best tapas bars. Hit spots like Bar del Pla, El Xampanyet, and Bodega Sepúlveda for vermouth, anchovies, croquetas, and pan con tomate. This is a perfect late-afternoon into evening activity that doubles as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Nomad Coffee Lab in El Born (if walking down early) or hotel breakfast. Budget €8–10.
meals.lunch: Light lunch during or after the architecture walk — grab a bocadillo or pintxos at a Gothic Quarter bar like Bar Marsella area or Kiosko Universal in La Boqueria market (€10–14). Avoid peak tourist traps inside La Boqueria.
meals.dinner: The Tapas & Vermouth Crawl in El Born effectively serves as dinner — budget €25–35 per person across multiple stops including drinks.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes as the cobblestones are uneven. El Born is very lively in the evening and transitions naturally into nightlife. This is a great night to stay out late and explore El Born's bar scene after the crawl.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning — sleep in or enjoy a slow breakfast. Head to the Barceloneta beach for a morning swim and a walk along the Passeig Marítim boardwalk. This is a great way to balance the busy architectural days with some rest and sun. The beach is about 25 minutes by Metro from Eixample (L4 Barceloneta stop).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the beach and freshen up at the hotel. In the mid-afternoon, visit Casa Milà (La Pedrera) — just steps from the hotel in Eixample — for a guided tour of the interior and the famous rooftop with its chimney sculptures. Book tickets in advance (€25–28). The rooftop is especially magical in the late afternoon light.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Night Concert — Attend an evening concert at this UNESCO-listed modernista masterpiece designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Check the concert schedule in advance and book tickets (€20–50 depending on performance). The stained-glass skylight and ornate interior are breathtaking when illuminated during a live performance. Located in El Born, easily reached by Metro.

meals.breakfast: Late breakfast or brunch at Brunch & Cake in Eixample — known for healthy, generous plates. Budget €12–16.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a chiringuito (beach bar) in Barceloneta — try fresh seafood, grilled fish, or a classic fideuà. Budget €18–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner near Palau de la Música in El Born — try Llamber or Bar del Pla for modern Catalan cuisine. Budget €25–35 per person. Aim for an early dinner (7:30–8:30 PM) before the concert.

day_by_day.notes: Check the Palau de la Música concert calendar at palaumusica.cat well in advance — August has a rich program. Dress smartly for the concert (smart casual is fine). La Pedrera rooftop also hosts evening 'Magic Nights' events with live music in summer — worth checking as an alternative.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — take a leisurely stroll along Passeig de Gràcia one last time to admire the Manzana de la Discordia (Block of Discord) with Casa Lleó Morera, Casa Amatller, and Casa Batlló side by side. Consider a quick visit inside Casa Batlló (book online, €35) for its extraordinary dragon-inspired interior if not yet visited. Pick up last-minute souvenirs at local design shops along the boulevard.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Montjuïc hill via cable car or funicular for panoramic views over Barcelona and the Mediterranean. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (€14) or simply enjoy the gardens and the view from the Castell de Montjuïc. A peaceful and scenic way to close the trip. Return to Eixample in the late afternoon to pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Eixample — splurge slightly on a special meal to celebrate the trip. Consider a reservation at Moments (Mandarin Oriental) for upscale Catalan cuisine, or keep it classic at Tragaluz in the Eixample design district. Afterward, one final drink at a rooftop bar to toast Barcelona's skyline.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Forn de Sant Jaume or a classic granja café in Eixample — try churros with chocolate or a traditional Catalan breakfast of pa amb tomàquet (bread with tomato). Budget €8–12.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a rooftop restaurant on Montjuïc or a café near the Fundació Joan Miró. Budget €15–20.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Tragaluz in Eixample — stylish, mid-to-upscale Mediterranean menu in a beautiful skylit space. Budget €35–50 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Check departure flight time and plan accordingly — if flying early the next morning, keep the evening relaxed and pack the night before. The Aerobus from Plaça de Catalunya (5-min walk from Eixample) runs to both T1 and T2 terminals and takes about 35 minutes. Validate your T-Casual metro card balance before leaving.

meals.dinner: Dinner at Disfrutar (2 Michelin stars) — one of Barcelona's most celebrated avant-garde restaurants. Book well in advance. Expect a tasting menu of creative, boundary-pushing Catalan cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book private airport transfer. Confirm Disfrutar reservation months ahead — it is one of the hardest tables to secure in Europe. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from travel.

day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter & El Born Architecture Walk: After lunch, join a small-group or private guided architectural walking tour through the medieval Gothic Quarter — exploring the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and Roman ruins — then transition into the trendy El Born neighborhood to admire the Santa Maria del Mar basilica and the Born Cultural Centre.
day_by_day.evening: Tapas & Vermouth Crawl in El Born: Seamlessly transition from the afternoon walk into an expert-led evening tapas and vermouth crawl through El Born's finest bars. Sample pintxos, jamón ibérico, anchovies, and local vermut at curated stops with insider access.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or at Faborit or Federal Café nearby — fresh pastries, eggs, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Xampanyet in El Born — a legendary cava bar and tapas spot. Order house cava, anchovies, and seasonal tapas in an authentic Catalan atmosphere.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bodega Sepúlveda or Cervecería Catalana — upscale tapas dining with an excellent wine list, conveniently located in Eixample near the hotel.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter tour — cobblestones can be uneven. Book the Sagrada Família private tour slot at least 2–3 months in advance for summer dates. Carry water as August heat can be intense.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Casa Batlló or Casa Milà (La Pedrera) with a premium guided experience — opt for the Magic Nights or exclusive early-access morning tour at La Pedrera for a more intimate visit. Explore Gaudí's fluid rooftop terrace, warrior chimneys, and stunning interior before the crowds arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Montjuïc: Take a private car or cable car up to Montjuïc hill. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró for world-class modern art, then stroll through the gardens with sweeping harbor views. Visit the Castell de Montjuïc for panoramic photography of the city and sea.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Night Concert: Attend an evening concert at this extraordinary UNESCO-listed Modernista masterpiece designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. The stained glass, sculptural details, and acoustic experience are unparalleled. Dress elegantly — this is a premium cultural highlight of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast or visit Mauri Pastisseria on Rambla de Catalunya — a historic Eixample patisserie with exquisite pastries and coffee since 1929.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Quimet & Quimet in Poble Sec (near Montjuïc) — a legendary standing-room-only bodega famous for creative montaditos and tinned seafood. Arrive early as it fills quickly.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert dinner at Hofmann — a refined Michelin-starred restaurant in El Born, a short walk from the Palau de la Música. Contemporary Catalan cuisine with impeccable service. Time dinner to finish 30 minutes before the concert.

day_by_day.notes: Check the Palau de la Música Catalana concert schedule in advance and book tickets as soon as available — premium seats sell out fast. Smart-casual to formal attire recommended for the concert. La Pedrera Magic Nights (evening rooftop experience) is an alternative if the concert timing doesn't align.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip or morning visit to Park Güell: Arrive at opening time (8:00 AM) for the Monumental Zone with a timed-entry ticket. Explore Gaudí's mosaic terraces, hypostyle room, and gingerbread gatehouses before the heat and crowds peak. Hire a private guide for in-depth architectural and historical context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta & Port Olímpic: Head down to the waterfront for a leisurely afternoon. Stroll along the Barceloneta promenade, visit the Barcelona Aquarium or the sculpture 'Peix d'Or' (Frank Gehry's golden fish). Consider a private luxury sailboat charter for 2–3 hours along the Costa Brava coastline — a premium highlight.
day_by_day.evening: Eixample Rooftop Bar Hopping (Round 2 — Nightlife Focus): Dive deeper into Barcelona's world-famous nightlife. Start with cocktails at Dry Martini Bar (a legendary Barcelona institution) in Eixample, then move to a rooftop bar for late-night views. End the night at Sala Apolo or Razzmatazz for live music or a premium club experience.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast before Park Güell — grab a croissant and coffee at a nearby café in Gràcia neighborhood, such as La Pepita.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at La Mar Salada near Barceloneta — excellent fresh seafood, paella, and rice dishes with sea views. A premium seafood experience steps from the beach.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tickets (Albert Adrià's avant-garde tapas bar) — a theatrical, creative dining experience inspired by circus and carnival themes. One of the most exciting restaurants in Barcelona. Book months in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Book the sailboat charter through a luxury concierge service or companies like Sailing BCN. Tickets restaurant requires reservations made exactly 2 months in advance via their online system — set a calendar reminder. Nightlife in Barcelona starts late — clubs typically peak between midnight and 3 AM.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana Architecture Tour (daytime): If not already visited, take the guided daytime tour of this Modernista jewel. Alternatively, visit the Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau — Domènech i Montaner's breathtaking former hospital complex, often less crowded than other landmarks and equally spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury Shopping & Farewell Stroll on Passeig de Gràcia: Spend the afternoon browsing Barcelona's most prestigious boulevard — visit flagship stores of Spanish designers, Loewe, and local artisan boutiques. Stop at Escribà patisseria for handcrafted chocolates and pastries to take home as gifts. Enjoy a final cava toast at a terrace bar.
